answers.explanation: People bring several devices each, and the network has its own devices too.
A separate subnet (and VLAN) lets the router enforce exactly what guests can reach.
Private space is free and plentiful, and NAT shares one public address.
Things others need to find at a fixed address. Everything else uses DHCP.
Size for the bursts. A link sized for the average is congested exactly when people need it.
Second octet the site, third octet the VLAN.
A /30 has exactly two usable addresses. (Many networks now use /31 for these links, per RFC 3021.)
